question: Which of the following is the most common application of plaster of Paris?

options.text: Creating casts for supporting fractured bones

solution:
The correct answer is __**Creating casts for supporting fractured bones**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plaster of Paris (POP) is primarily used to create orthopedic casts for immobilizing fractured bones during the healing process.
 
• It is favored in medical applications due to its quick-setting properties and ability to conform to the shape of the body part being treated.
 
• POP is applied as a bandage soaked in water which then hardens to form a sturdy support structure around the injured area.
 
• Orthopedic casts made from POP are critical in ensuring proper alignment and stabilization of bones to facilitate effective healing.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Composition of Plaster of Paris**

 
 
• Plaster of Paris is chemically known as calcium sulfate hemihydrate (CaSO4·½H2O).
 
• It is produced by heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) to about 150°C to remove water molecules.
 
 
 
• **Other Uses of Plaster of Paris**
 
 
• Besides medical applications, POP is used in art for making sculptures and decorative elements.
 
• It is also employed in the construction industry for creating false ceilings and coating walls.
 
 
 
• **Handling and Safety**
 
 
• POP should be handled with care, as it can cause skin irritation and respiratory issues if inhaled as dust.
 
• It is important to use protective gear such as gloves and masks when working with POP.
 
 
 
• **Setting and Hardening Process**
 
 
• When mixed with water, POP undergoes an exothermic reaction, causing it to set and harden quickly.
 
• The setting time can be adjusted by altering the temperature and the amount of water used.
